(Greenville, South Carolina) | college = [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–2025 | team3 = [[Capital City Go-Go]] | years4 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team4 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | years5 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team5 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | highlights = }} '''John Erik Butler Jr.''' (born December 4, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. ==High school career== Butler played basketball for [[Christ Church Episcopal School]] in [[Greenville, South Carolina]], where he was coached by his father, John Sr., and was teammates with his younger brother, Jordan.{{cite web|first=Geoff|last=Preston|title=Standing tall: How Christ Church Butler brothers juggle public eye and basketball pressure|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/02/18/christ-church-basketball-brothers-john-butler-jordan-help-cavaliers-raise-bar/2675588001/|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=February 18, 2020|access-date=June 19, 2022}} As a senior, he averaged 20.1 points, 8.5 rebounds and 2.9 blocks per game, earning Upstate Player of the Year honors from ''[[The Greenville News]]''.{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Dandron|title=Former Christ Church star John Butler Jr. leads Florida State upset of No. 5 Duke|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2022/01/19/former-christ-church-star-helps-florida-state-basketball-upset-no-6-duke/6578453001/|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=January 19, 2022|access-date=June 19, 2022}} Butler was named Class 2A Player of the Year and led his team to the state championship.{{cite web|first=Bob|last=Ferrante|title=Butler grew up, grew comfortable with his shot, embracing FSU|url=https://theosceola.com/butler-grew-up-grew-comfortable-with-his-shot-embracing-fsu/|website=TheOsceola.com|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=June 19, 2022}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] over offers from [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]] and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web|first=Geoff|last=Preston|title=Christ Church basketball star John Butler Jr. commits to Florida State|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/29/christ-church-star-john-butler-jr-commits-florida-state-basketball/5528627002/|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=July 29, 2020|access-date=June 19, 2022}} ==College career== On March 2, 2022, Butler recorded a career-high 16 points, eight rebounds and four blocks in a 74–70 win against [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]].{{cite web|title=John Butler helps host FSU thwart Notre Dame|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-state-seminoles/os-sp-fsu-notre-dame-mens-basketball-0303-20220303-f2aklpbeobeszoejduvysghokq-story.html|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 2, 2022|access-date=June 19, 2022}} As a freshman, he averaged 5.9 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game, shooting 39.3 percent from three-point range. Butler declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] and opted to forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite magazine|first=Austin|last=Veazey|title=John Butler makes NBA Draft decision|url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/basketball/john-butler-makes-nba-draft-decision|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 1, 2022|access-date=June 19, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the 2022 NBA draft, Butler joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for [[NBA Summer League]] play.{{cite news|first=Pete|last=Yanity|title=Butler looks to fit with Pelicans|url=https://www.wspa.com/sports/nba/butler-looks-to-fit-with-pelicans/|work=WSPA|date=July 9, 2022|access-date=August 2, 2022}} On October 3, 2022, he was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the Pelicans for the 22–23 season. However, he was waived on October 10.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Kelan Martin and Javonte Smart|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-kelan-martin-javonte-smart-roster-101022|website=NBA.com|date=October 10, 2022|access-date=October 10, 2022}} On October 20, 2022, Butler signed a two-way contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]],{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign John Butler Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-john-butler-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2022|access-date=March 17, 2023}} and on February 26, 2023, he was assigned to the [[Stockton Kings]] by the Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=Portland Trail Blazers Flex-Transfer John Butler Jr. to Stockton Kings|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/portland-trail-blazers-flex-transfer-john-butler-jr-to-stockton-kings|website=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2023|access-date=February 26, 2023}} On July 6, 2023, Butler signed another two-way contract with the Blazers,{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Ibou Badji And John Butler Jr. To Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-re-sign-ibou-badji-and-john-butler-jr-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023}} but was waived on October 21.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Convert Justin Minaya To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-convert-justin-minaya-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}} ===Capital City Go-Go (2023–2025)=== On October 23, 2023, Butler signed a two-way contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign John Butler Jr. To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-john-butler-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2023|access-date=October 28, 2023}} However, he was waived on December 8,{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Jules Bernard to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-jules-bernard-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} after appearing in nine games with the [[Capital City Go-Go]], Washington's [[NBA G League]] affiliate.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Wizards Waive John Butler Jr.|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/12/wizards-to-waive-john-butler-jr.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 8, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} On December 10, he rejoined Capital City.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Capital City Go-Go Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Capital-City-Go-Go/55/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 11, 2023}} On October 13, 2024, re-signed with the Wizards,{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=Official: The Washington Wizards have signed F Taylor Funk and F/C John Butler Jr. to Exhibit 10 contracts.|number=1845479094156247167|user=WizPRStats|date=October 13, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}} but was waived six days later.{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=The Washington Wizards have waived F/C John Butler Jr., F Taylor Funk, and F Mouhamadou Gueye.|number=1847632826448978076|user=WizPRStats|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Albert|last=Lee|title=Wizards waive John Butler, Jr., Funk and Gueye|url=https://www.bulletsforever.com/2024/10/19/24274231/washington-wizards-john-butler-jr-taylor-funk-mouhamadou-gueye|website=BulletsForever.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}} On October 28, he rejoined the Go-Go.{{cite web|title=Go-Go Announce Training Camp Roster, Dates|url=https://capitalcity.gleague.nba.com/news/go-go-announce-training-camp-roster-dates-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} ===Wisconsin Herd (2025–2026)=== On March 6th, 2025, Butler was traded to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] for the returning rights of [[Darryl Morsell]], a 2026 G-League Draft first round, and a second round pick. On November 7, 2025, Butler was named to the [[Wisconsin Herd]] opening night roster.{{cite web|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2025-26-opening-night-roster|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2025-26 OPENING NIGHT ROSTER|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 7, 2025|access-date=November 7, 2025}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2026–present)=== On September 4, 2026, Butler signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign John Butler Jr.
